limitations.statement: Theorem 5.1 statement is visible, but its Proof is deferred by the proceedings PDF to the separate full paper. This proposal carries no performance certification or structured performance dependency.

One-coordinate derivative feedback does not imply sparse iterates: convex combinations and z updates involve vectors. No unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound or support/output restriction is asserted.

variants.cost: Exactly T selected-coordinate derivative queries, reused between the two updates. Separately charge forming S and probabilities, sampling, vector arithmetic and storage. A direct dense implementation uses O(n) initialization/storage and O(n) arithmetic per iteration; these are implementation accounting, not a source theorem about optimized runtime. No acquisition cost for L_i or sigma is included; they are public inputs. No objective or full-gradient query is prescribed.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Source PDF page 5, Algorithm 1 lines 1–11 and Section 5; beta=0 specialization.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 with beta=0
variants.output: Return y_T; for T=0 return x0.
public_inputs: n≥1, continuously differentiable convex f:R^n→R, initial x0∈R^n, integer T≥0
Positive coordinate smoothness bounds L_1,...,L_n and positive Euclidean strong-convexity parameter sigma
variants.query_and_update: For k=0,...,T−1: form x_{k+1}=tau z_k+(1−tau)y_k. Sample i with conditional probability p_i. Query g=∂_i f(x_{k+1}) once and reuse it. Set y_{k+1}=x_{k+1}−(g/L_i)e_i and z_{k+1}=(z_k+eta sigma x_{k+1}−(eta/p_i)g e_i)/(1+eta sigma). Both updates use the old z_k and the same x_{k+1},i,g.
variants.requirements: For all x,y∈R^n, f(y)≥f(x)+<∇f(x),y−x>+(sigma/2)||y−x||_2^2. For every x, delta>0 and coordinate i, |∂_i f(x+delta e_i)−∂_i f(x)|≤L_i delta. Access exact selected coordinate derivatives and vector arithmetic. This is an unconstrained smooth objective; a separate nonsmooth proximal term is not covered.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set S=sum_i sqrt(L_i), p_i=sqrt(L_i)/S, tau=2/(1+sqrt(1+4S^2/sigma)), eta=1/(tau S^2). Initialize y_0=z_0=x0.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use the fixed tau and eta above, derived from public L_i and sigma. Stop after the supplied T iterations. No adaptive accuracy certificate or objective evaluation is required by these rules.
